seo_meta_description: Master Basics on the Digital SAT using built-in Desmos graphing calculator hacks, syntax commands, regressions, and speed drills.
exam_weightage: Essential Digital SAT Tool (5-8 Questions per Module)

techniques.title: Variable Substitution with Sliders
techniques.description: Define variables as constants to evaluate complex expressions instantly without manual arithmetic.
techniques.when_to_use: When a problem provides specific values for variables and asks for the result of an expression.
techniques.pro_tip: Type the expression exactly as it appears in the prompt; Desmos will output the value immediately.

techniques.title: Intersection Point Finder
techniques.description: Graph two functions and click the point where they cross to find the solution (x, y).
techniques.when_to_use: Systems of equations or finding where two lines/curves meet.
techniques.pro_tip: Click the grey dot that appears at the intersection to see the coordinates.

techniques.title: Table-Based Regression
techniques.description: Input data points into a table and use the tilde (~) operator to find the line of best fit.
techniques.when_to_use: Linear modeling or finding the equation of a line given two or more points.
techniques.pro_tip: Use the 'y1' and 'x1' syntax exactly as shown in the table headers.

techniques.title: Solving Equations via X-Intercepts
techniques.description: Set an equation to zero and find the x-intercepts to solve for x.
techniques.when_to_use: Any equation where you need to find the value of x.
techniques.pro_tip: If the equation is complex, move everything to one side so it equals zero, then graph.

techniques.title: Evaluating Functions at Points
techniques.description: Define a function using f(x) notation, then type f(number) to evaluate.
techniques.pro_tip: You can define multiple functions like f(x) and g(x) and perform operations like f(x) + g(x).

speed_walkthroughs.problem: If $3x + 4 = 19$, what is the value of $x$?
desmos_hack: Click the vertical line that appears at x = 5

drills.question: If $f(x) = 2x^2 - 5$, what is the value of $f(3)$?
explanation: Define the function f(x) in the first line.
Type f(3) in the second line to get the result 13.

drills.question: What is the solution to the system $y = 2x + 1$ and $y = -x + 4$?
explanation: The question asks for the x-value, which is 1.
